name: or

phase_0.boundary_condition: The closed system of Boolean algebra containing the OR operation and its truth table

VINIT.justification: Before any inputs are applied, the system is void of determinate truth values.

TANCH.justification: Defines the complete set of truth values and the rules that contain the OR operation.

AFWD.justification: Transmits input voltages through the gate to produce an output according to OR semantics.

AREV.justification: Maps an output truth value to the set of input pairs that could produce it, reversing the morphism.

CLINK.justification: Chains multiple OR operations in sequence, composing their input-output transformations.

IMSCRIB.justification: The operation OR(x,x) = x, showing self-reference; also the gate recognizes its own function.

FSPLIT.justification: Splits the OR function into two subfunctions: one for when the first input is true, one for when it is false.

FFUSE.justification: Recombines the two subfunctions under the condition of the first input, recovering the original OR function.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative evaluation: if first input is 1, output is 1 regardless of second input.

EVALF.justification: Negative evaluation: if first input is 0, output equals the second input.

ENGAGR.justification: A paradice where the first input is simultaneously 0 and 1, held without resolution; no stable output.

IFIX.justification: Permanent, append-only fixation of the OR gate's truth table in hardware or reference memory.

split_outputs: branch: first input true → output always 1
branch: first input false → output equals second input

phase_3.both_description: 11: inputs contradictory, output in paradice (both held simultaneously)

steps.domain_action: initialize void state with no gate inputs
define the Boolean algebra that contains the OR operation
enable forward signal propagation through the gate
decompose the OR function into two conditional subfunctions based on the first input
evaluate the true branch where first input is 1, output is 1
evaluate the false branch where first input is 0, output equals second input
recombine the two branches under the condition of the first input, recovering the OR function
record the self-identity property OR(x,x) = x
compose the OR operation with a subsequent gate in sequence
perform reverse inference from output to input possibilities
hold the contradictory input state where first input is both 0 and 1
permanently record the OR truth table

phase_5.compiler_frontend: truth-table compiler that translates gate specifications into Boolean expressions
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: signal wires carrying voltage levels between gates
phase_5.memory_mechanism: latch circuits storing intermediate truth values
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: clock-driven evaluation order for sequential composition
phase_5.alfs_store: canonical reference table of all binary logical operations

phase_6.cycle_cost: one voltage transition per input change
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: stable input voltages at gate terminals
phase_6.post_cycle_state: stable output voltage at gate terminal
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the gate is conservative; no thermodynamic irreversibility in ideal logic
